restaurant.text: India restaurant serving Royal Indian Cuisine. Live Ghazal performances. A Private dining room is available for up to 12 persons and an intimate bar for pre-dinner drinks.

photo.name: Madhavaram Botanical Garden
photo.text: The largest botanical garden, set up by the Department of Horticulture in 2018. The garden is broadly divided into sections for fruits, medicinal plants, indoor plants, cacti and ornamental arboretum, besides one for protected cultivation.

photo.name: Chepauk Palace
photo.text: The building near Marina Beach in Indo-Saracenic style was the official residence of the Nawab of Arcot from 1768 to 1855,.

photo.name: Pulhal Lake
photo.text: A British-era reservoir built in 1876. There are two masonry weirs in the reservoir.

photo.name: Marina Beach
photo.area: Water Land Drive Rd, Valmiki Nagar, Netaji Nagar
photo.text: This is long and offers excellent opportunities for walks and has a very wide sandy foreshore. Its width is up to. Marina Beach is the second-longest beach in the world after Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh. it is an elegant promenade with flower beds along its lanes.

photo.name: Breezy Beach
photo.area: Water Land Drive Rd, Lakshmana Perumal Nagar, Valmiki Nagar
photo.text: It is smaller and less popular than Elliot's Beach. This beach is not as commercialised as Elliot's Beach and is hence more quiet and peaceful. Evenings are delightful and with gentle breezy here, Lots of tourists are attracted towards this beach.
photo.image: India - Chennai - Valmiki Nagar beach looking north (2278424111).jpg

photo.name: Edward Elliot's Beach
photo.text: This is spread along the coast down south from the Marina Beach. It is also the night beach for Chennai youth. This beach is comparatively quieter. At the end of this beach are the Velankanni church and the Ashtalakshmi temple.

photo.name: Golden Beach
photo.text: The first amusement park in Chennai, just about 11 km away from Adyar. Still a landmark of Chennai, this park offers over 40 odd rides for the fun seeker.

Hyderabad.name: Hyderabad
Hyderabad.tagline: Hyderabad,, the "Pearl City", is the capital of the state of Telangana.

info.intro: Hyderabad,, the "Pearl City", is the capital of the state of Telangana. Founded in the late 16th century on the hot and dry Deccan Plateau, Hyderabad is a city replete with history and traditions, as well as the wonderful palaces, mosques, bazaars, lakes and other heritage sites in the city. One of the most populous cities in Southern India, the modern-day Hyderabad is the result of the amalgamation with its twin city Secunderabad across the Hussain Sagar lake, a former British enclave during the city's Nizam rule. With the expansion of Cyberabad to the west, the city now competes with Bengaluru, Gurugram and Pune for the crown of India's IT capital.
info.understand: If you are visiting Hyderabad on business, it is easy to miss the 400-year-old city. The one that immediately hits the eye is a sprawling metropolis of shopping malls and office buildings with glass façades. The magnificent "old city" that was once the seat of the Nizam, the ruler of the largest and the most opulent princely state, and the twin city of Secunderabad where the British maintained a cantonment to keep the army within striking distance of the Nizam, can be seen only if you take the time out to see them. Name The name "Hyderabad" literally means "Lion City" in Persian. A popular legend suggests that the founder of the city, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, named it "Bhagyanagar" ("Fortunate City") after Bhagmati, a Telugu courtesan he had an affair with. After she converted to Islam and took on the name of "Hyder Mahal", he renamed the city to "Hyderabad".
info.get_in: As you would expect from a major international airport, there is good domestic as well as international connectivity from many locations. It is far from the city, and with the exception of Novotel, there aren't any good hotels close by. Road connectivity to the city is excellent, though. The Nehru Outer Ring Road Expressway connects to the airport - take exit 16. The P V Narasimha Rao Expressway connects the airport with Mehdipattnam in South Hyderabad. There are multiple options to get into the city. The Pushpak - Airport Liner, an air-conditioned bus service operated by the Telangana government, goes to various designated points - Secunderabad (Jubilee Bus Station), Miyapur, BHEL and the Mahatma Gandhi Bus terminal (Imlibun) near Charminar. These routes cover most major areas of the city. The airport website has detailed information about pickup and stop points, along with timings.
info.get_around: Hyderabad's public transport options have been increasing over the years. It has an overcrowded bus network and a rudimentary local train network. In the past 5 years, it has had its own elevated metro rail service that provides fast and cheap connectivity to some areas. The ubiquitous yellow and black auto-rickshaws have now been supplemented by the app-based taxi services that provide fairly good service all over the city. Driving yourself around the city may be an excellent option or a terrible choice, depending on which areas you want to go to, and how comfortable you are with other people driving like utter lunatics. The Hyderabad Metro is a fast, clean and efficient mode of travel, and is better than driving or taking a cab for the areas it serves. Trains run at every 4 minutes from early morning to late in the night. The trains run on an elevated corridor.
info.stay_safe: Hyderabad used to suffer from terrorism between 2007 and 2013. There were bomb blasts at Mecca Masjid, Lumbini Park, places often frequented by travellers and also at busy marketplaces. Since the city is free of terrorism since 2014, the chances that you will be in danger are quite low. However, you should still make your own risk assessment, as the intrusive security will more likely dampen your enjoyment of your Hyderabad vacation than any physical danger. Every shopping mall, theatre and palace has metal detectors and security guards patting you down. The Old City used to be a communally sensitive zone, and a venue for religiously aggravated riots between Hindus and Muslims. It was common for the police to impose a curfew in that area while the rest of the city went about life without any problems.

attraction.name: Charminar
attraction.area: take an auto (₹25) or walk from (about 25 minutes)
attraction.text: Literally "four minarets" (char means "four" and minar means "minaret"). Quli Qutb Shah built the Charminar in 1591 at the very spot at which he prayed to end the plague epidemic. The Charminar, made of pulverised marble, limestone, mortar and granite, has long been the icon of Hyderabad.
attraction.hours: Mon–Sat 9AM–5PM, closed on Fri 1–2PM for prayers
attraction.price: ₹25, Children below 11 free (for Indians), ₹300 (for foreigners), video cameras...

attraction.name: Mahboob Chowk Clock Tower
attraction.text: A five-storied architectural clock tower which was built in 1892. The clock tower is erected in the midst of the small garden; it has four large clocks on its sides which enable the time to be seen from any direction. The clock tower is designed in the Turkish style.

attraction.name: The Palmetum, Malakpet
attraction.text: It is a specialised botanical garden, which features only one family of plants: the palms. The garden's collection contains all six subfamilies within the family Arecaceae, with a total of about 120 varieties of 250 trees.

attraction.name: Purana pul
attraction.text: The first bridge ever constructed in Hyderabad. It was built over the Musi River in 1578 during the Qutb Shahi dynasty in order to connect Golconda and Hyderabad.

attraction.name: Telangana High Court
attraction.text: Founded by the 7th Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan as the High Court of Hyderabad. This is one of the finest buildings in the city, built in red and white stones in Saracenic style. The plan of the high court was drawn up by Shankar Lal of Jaipur and the local engineer who executed the design was Mehar Ali Fazil.

attraction.name: Badshahi Ashurkhana
attraction.text: A mourning place for Shia Muslims, built in 1594.

attraction.name: Armenian Cemetery
attraction.text: The four hundred cemetery houses a total of 20 graves (19 Armenian and 1 Dutch). The cemetery consists of a series of scattered graves with no pattern. Both the pavilions house several graves, probably from the same family. The cemetery is not maintained and often locked.

attraction.name: Paigah Tombs
attraction.text: These tombs belong to the 'Paigah' nobles (tied by blood and marriage to the Nizams) and are about 200 years old. These unique lime and mortar tombs are beautifully carved and have marble inlay work on them. Relaxing environment with bird singing.

attraction.name: Raymond Tomb
attraction.text: Michel Raymond, a French mercenary, was a military commander in the service of the second Nizam and also his close friend. He died in 1798 and was buried on top of a hillock at Tirumala Hills, Malakpet.

attraction.name: Chowmahalla Palace
attraction.text: It was the seat of the Asaf Jahi dynasty where the Nizam entertained his official guests and royal visitors. The palace consists of a row of four courtyards, with a grand pillared Durbar Hall in the centre.

attraction.name: Khursheed Jah Devdi
attraction.text: A European styled architectural palace, once home to the Paigah nobles. The palace is in shambles as of 2017 due to neglect. The gardens blossomed with flowers and fountains making the ambiance livelier.

attraction.name: Purani Haveli
attraction.text: It was originally the palace of the Nizam's Prime Minister. It was later renovated and became the quarters of the Nizam's son. It is a U-shaped complex with a single-storeyed building in the European style. The palace also houses the Nizam Museum, which is dedicated to the last Nizam of Hyderabad.

restaurant.name: The Water Front
restaurant.text: Has a nice view of Hussain Sagar lake, but the food, at its best, is passable.

restaurant.name: Ofen
restaurant.area: Plot Number 49, Road Number 10, Banjara Hills
restaurant.text: Excellent place for breads and related foods - especially for health conscious. Includes breads like whole grain breads, ragi breads and sugar free cakes.

restaurant.name: King & Cardinal
restaurant.text: Pizzas and burgers. Also serves Indian Chinese snacks.

restaurant.name: Hyderabadi dum biryani
restaurant.text: Dum refers to the baking process and basmati rice and meat or vegetables are mixed in a pot and heated for a long time. During the Nizam's time, the biryani was made with goat carefully cooked with rice.

restaurant.name: Falooda
restaurant.text: A favourite drink of Hyderabad.

restaurant.name: Gosht
restaurant.text: Made from a buck/billy/young goat, and is associated with the Hyderabadi cuisine. Hyderabadis prize the meat of a male goat.

restaurant.name: Hyderabadi Haleem
restaurant.text: A dish that is available only during the month of Ramadaan (Ramzan).

restaurant.name: Mirchi ka salan
restaurant.text: Is another dish that serves as a tasty accompaniment to any rice dish, it is served with spicy chilli sauce.

restaurant.name: Raghu pan shop
restaurant.text: Popular for Calcutta menakshi and Meetha Pan, available all the time during work hours.

restaurant.name: Sanman Hotel
restaurant.text: Cheap. For take away, ask at the parcel counter.

restaurant.name: Sandarshini
restaurant.text: Delicious South Indian dishes. Had over 5 locations

restaurant.name: Shadaab
restaurant.text: Famous for its Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani and Jabda Gosht available only in the morning, served for breakfast.

cafe.name: Osmania biscuits
cafe.text: Drinking Irani chai is incomplete without Osmania biscuits. It is a traditional Hyderabadi treat made from Kesar strands, milk, flour, butter, sugar and salt.

cafe.name: Hyderabad House
cafe.text: This is a chain of restaurants, serving Hyderabadi style food all over the city. There are also outlets that comprise just a takeaway counter. Try the Lukhmi. Vegetarians will have few choices.

cafe.name: Nimrah Cafe & Bakery
cafe.area: Shop No 20 - 4 - 1238 Champapet Main Road, Charminar
cafe.text: The most well-known cafe selling Irani chai and Osmania biscuits in Hyderabad. Very crowded.

cafe.name: Double Ka Meetha
cafe.text: A dessert made from bread, milk and dry fruits.

cafe.name: Irani chai
cafe.text: This is the tea of Hyderabad, available at any of the ubiquitous "Chai" shops. However, not all of them have the best hygiene and it is best to go with a local. The crowd at the stalls is composed mainly of blue-collar workers and college students so expect a noisy environment with conversational topics that range...

cafe.name: Khubani ka meetha
cafe.text: Hyderabad's preferred dessert sweet. It is made from apricots boiled in sugar syrup till they achieve a thick consistency. It looks similar to but tastes different from gajar ka halwa (carrot halwa). It is often topped with ice cream or cream.

cafe.name: Bowl O'China
cafe.text: This is a chain restaurant started by the same people who run Hyderabad House. Has multiple locations in the city. Average Indian Chinese food.

cafe.name: Minerva Coffee Shop
cafe.text: Bit of a local institution, serving tasty vegetarian South and North Indian snacks and food. has 4 locations.

cafe.name: Deli 9
cafe.text: Bakery and cafe. Cakes, pastries, quiches and puffs. 2 locations.

cafe.name: Pulla Reddy Sweets
cafe.text: is a chain of sweet shops. The outlets are found all over Hyderabad and are so popular that it has spawned imitators who copy the distinctive yellow signs and choose some variation of "Reddy" (a common last name in Andhra Pradesh) as the name.

cafe.name: Pista House
cafe.text: Famous bakery in Hyderabad serving world famous haleem which is only available during Ramadan.

cafe.name: Cafe Bahaar
cafe.area: Opp. Commissioner Office, Old MLA Quarters, Basheerbagh
cafe.text: Biryanis and meat curries, moderately priced.

photo.name: Mahboob Chowk Clock Tower
photo.text: A five-storied architectural clock tower which was built in 1892. The clock tower is erected in the midst of the small garden; it has four large clocks on its sides which enable the time to be seen from any direction. The clock tower is designed in the Turkish style.

photo.name: The Palmetum, Malakpet
photo.text: It is a specialised botanical garden, which features only one family of plants: the palms. The garden's collection contains all six subfamilies within the family Arecaceae, with a total of about 120 varieties of 250 trees.

photo.name: Hussain Sagar
photo.text: The artificial lake is a historical landmark, built during the reign of Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah in 1562 by damming the Musi. This forms the boundary between Hyderabad and Secunderabad. Surrounding the lake are various parks, temples, statues and historical buildings. This is one of the few walkable places in the city.

photo.name: Lumbini Park
photo.text: See water cascades, go on guided car rides. Go on a boat ride and see the Buddha statue at the centre of the lake. It also offers nice Laser Shows in the evening which is first in India.

photo.name: Public Gardens
photo.text: Known as the Bagh-e-aam (Garden for the commoners), it has well laid-out gardens and is surrounded by the imposing State Legislative Assembly building, the Jubilee Hall, the Jawahar Bal Bhavan, the Health Museum and the State Archaeological Museum.

photo.name: Shamirpet Lake
photo.area: 24 km away to the north of Secunderabad
photo.text: Shamirpet has a beautiful lake and a deer park. The peaceful environs make it a great picnic spot. Telangana Tourism offers comfortable cottages facilities for accommodation (under private management), while the forest lodge can be booked with the Telangana Forest Department office at Saifabad.

photo.name: Kotla Vijayabhaskara Reddy Botanical Garden
photo.text: Tents are available for longer visits. The paved walkways take you through the 19 sections (Vanaja) in the Patil. The bamboo and palm sectors are major attractions, with varieties of bamboo trees separated by a 3-metre (10 ft) distance.

photo.name: Ameenpur Lake
photo.text: A major sport for birdwatchers, with various resident and migratory birds like flamingos, egrets, herons, cormorants, kingfishers and river terns.

photo.name: Light and Sound Show
photo.text: After sunset, there is an hour-long light and sound show telling you the story of the Golconda Fort which is worth seeing, though it could be a little boring. The English show runs Nov-Feb 6:30PM daily and Mar-Oct until 7PM daily. Hindi and Telugu shows are run afterwards on certain days.
photo.price: Price for foreigners ₹50/100 for normal/executive tickets

Kathmandu.name: Kathmandu
Kathmandu.tagline: Kathmandu is the largest city and capital of Nepal, and the namesake of the Kathmandu Valley.

info.intro: Kathmandu is the largest city and capital of Nepal, and the namesake of the Kathmandu Valley. Once thought to be the fabled and inaccessible Shangri-La, Kathmandu is a fast-growing spot catering to a wide range of holiday types and budgets. As a result of considerable urban growth in recent decades, it is now part of one continuous urban area together with Patan to the south.
info.understand: According to a census conducted in 2011, Kathmandu metropolis has 2.5 million inhabitants, and the agglomeration has a population of more than 3 million inhabitants. The metropolitan city area is 50.67 km (19.56 sq mi) and has a population density of 3000 per km and 17,000 per km square in the city proper. The city stands at an elevation of approximately 1,400 metres (4,600 ft) in the bowl-shaped Kathmandu Valley of central Nepal. It is surrounded by four major mountains: Shivapuri, Phulchoki, Nagarjun, and Chandragiri. Kathmandu Valley is part of three districts (Kathmandu, Lalitpur, and Bhaktapur), has the highest population density in the country, and is home to about a twelfth of Nepal's population. Historically, the Kathmandu Valley and adjoining areas were known as Nepal Mandala.
info.get_in: By plane Tourist SIM cards are available at two counters, which are located between immigration and customs. International flights Most international flights to Kathmandu arrive from Delhi, UAE, Qatar, or Bangkok. International airlines serving Kathmandu include: Biman Bangladesh Airlines - Dhaka Air Arabia - Sharjah. Air China - Chengdu. Air Asia - Kuala Lumpur. Fly Dubai - Dubai. Druk Air - Paro and Delhi Etihad Airways - Abu Dhabi. Gulf Air - Bahrain. Air India - Delhi and Kolkata. Korean Air - Seoul.Nepal Airlines - Bangkok, Delhi, Dubai, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Osaka, Singapore and Shanghai. Singapore Airlines - Singapore. Thai Airways - Bangkok. Qatar Airways - Doha. China Southern Airlines - Guangzhou. China Eastern Airlines - Kunming. Turkish Airlines - Istanbul. Malaysian Airlines- Kuala Lumpur.
info.get_around: If you fly in, be sure to pick up a free Kathmandu Valley map at the airport. The first thing some visitors notice about Kathmandu is the general lack of house numbers and street names except for major roads such as Tri Devi & Ring Road (loops around the city). In most cases directions are given relative to the nearest chowk or tole (an intersection or square, often with a market) or a noteworthy location or building (such as a temple or restaurant). In the tourist district of Thamel, the Kathmandu Guest House is the main landmark. Most of the sites of interest are near the stupa and can easily be reached on foot. Taxis are available on the main road by the main stupa gate, until around 9PM. The alleys around the stupa are packed with small shops and cafes, and the best way to explore them is on foot. However, be aware of two-wheelers.
info.stay_safe: Canadian Consular Affairs, the UK Foreign and Commonwealth office, and the US State Department provide travel advice. Nepal is safe to visit but caution must be taken. After the Maoists joined the government in about 2006, Nepal become relatively peaceful and more stable. However, visitors should avoid public demonstrations and may want to register with their consulate on arrival. Although tourists haven't been directly targeted by politically motivated violence, it is possible to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. The frequent strikes, locally known as bandh or banda, that are still held on occasion, are a major inconvenience for most tourists as all transportation stops, and many shops and restaurants close. In the 10-day period leading up to the Constituent Assembly Elections in November 2013.

attraction.name: Boudha Stupa
attraction.text: According to legend, Boudhanath Stupa was built in the 5th century AD by an elderly poultry woman who sought land from the king to construct a shrine to the Buddha. The king agreed, offering her as much land as she could cover with the skin of a water buffalo.
attraction.price: Foreigners pay Rs400, but this can be waived for guests of hotels at the other...

attraction.name: Pashupatinath Temple
attraction.area: 20-minute walk past several temples from Boudhanath
attraction.text: This important Hindu temple is dedicated to Shiva in his form as the Lord of the Beasts. While only Hindus are allowed to enter the inner sanctum, the surrounding temple grounds are open to all visitors.
attraction.image: 2023 January night aarti at Pashupatinath Temple, Kathmandu 02.jpg

attraction.name: Taragaon Museum
attraction.text: turn it into a do umentation centre documenting what artists, photographers, architects, anthropologists and Samskritists from abroad had contributed in the second half of the 20th century to identify, highlight and preserve the cultural heritage of the Kathmandu Valley.

attraction.name: Guhyeshwari Temple
attraction.text: One of the Shakti Peethas of Nepal, considered auspicious to Shakti devotees.

attraction.name: Matrikeshwor Mahadev
attraction.text: Middle of Rani Pokhari Pond

attraction.name: Narayanhiti Palace Museum
attraction.area: in the north-central part of Kathmandu
attraction.text: Narayanhiti comes from Narayana, a form of the Hindu god Lord Vishnu, and Hiti, meaning "water spout" (Vishnu's temple is located opposite the palace, and the water spout is located east of the main entrance to the precinct).

attraction.name: Nepal Art Council Gallery
attraction.area: in the Babar Mahal, on the way to Tribhuvan International Airport
attraction.text: This gallery contains artwork of both national and international artists and extensive halls regularly used for art exhibitions

attraction.name: Swayambhunath
attraction.text: Perched on a hill overlooking Kathmandu, Swayambhu is a revered site featuring a grand stupa surrounded by Buddhist and Hindu iconography. According to legend, a former Buddha visited the valley, which was then a vast lake.
attraction.price: Foreigners: Rs200 for single entry; Rs750 for a multiple entry pass

attraction.name: Garden of Dreams
attraction.text: Relax in this beautiful and peaceful walled garden close to Thamel and the former Royal Palace. Beautifully renovated in partnership with the Austrian government. It has two pavilions depicting two of the six annual seasons in the Hindu calendar. There is a mini exhibition showing old photos of this garden.
attraction.price: Rs400 for non-Nepalese, Rs150 for Nepalese

attraction.name: Kasthamandap
attraction.area: southwest side of the Square, actually this is the Maru Square
attraction.text: A three-storey temple enshrining an image of Gorakhnath. It was built in the 16th century in pagoda style. The name of Kathmandu is a derivative of the word Kasthamandap. It was built under the reign of King Laxmi Narsingha Malla. It was built as a rest house for travelers.

attraction.name: National Museum
attraction.text: This in an historical building. It was constructed in the early 19th century by General Bhimsen Thapa. It is the most important museum in the country, housing an extensive collection of weapons, art and antiquities of historic and cultural importance.

attraction.name: Tribhuvan Museum
attraction.text: contains artifacts related to the King Tribhuvan. It has a variety of pieces including his personal belongings, letters and papers, memorabilia related to events he was involved in and a rare collection of photos and paintings of the Royal family.

restaurant.name: Helena's Rooftop Restaurant
restaurant.text: Excellent food, great service, and modest prices. It is claimed to have the tallest rooftop restaurant in Kathmandu, and the views from there of the city, especially at night, are reported to be worth the climb. Serves Western and regional cuisine.
restaurant.price: chicken tikka masala costs around Rs350

restaurant.name: New Orleans
restaurant.text: A good variety of well-made food, including pasta, Nepali and salads. Pleasant Newari courtyard setting

restaurant.name: Rum Doodle
restaurant.text: Excellent food at modest prices, including live music on most nights. Carry on straight past Helena's, around the "chicane", where the road bends then straightens out again, and turn the next right. It is signposted but the sign's fairly small. Everest summiteers can eat here for free. Extraphone=+977-1-4248692

restaurant.name: Thamel House Restaurant
restaurant.text: Nepali and Newari cuisine. There is a cultural show every evening from 19:00.

restaurant.name: Stupa Dining Restaurant With Garden
restaurant.area: Boudha, Dhara Tole, before turning to Hyatt Road
restaurant.text: Local restaurant with good, clean, cheap food, and with live music.

restaurant.name: Bawarchi
restaurant.text: Superb Indian and Chinese food, specializing in kathi rolls which are a fried, flat bread wrap with spicy meat, paneer or veg filling. Great for lunchtime snacks or evening meals.

restaurant.name: Chez Caroline.
restaurant.text: Just off the main Thapathali junction, near the old parliament building. Excellent French food and salads. 700-900 for a main. Ask a taxi driver to find it.

restaurant.name: Mike's Breakfast
restaurant.text: Lazimpat Near Standard Chartered. A brisk 15 minute walk from Thamel Taxi Stand, but confusing with one-way streets. Good pancakes alongside with other meals. Mostly outdoor tables under bamboo shelters + available indoor screened dining.

restaurant.name: New Natraj Tandoori
restaurant.text: Cheap, plentiful and delicious Indian food. Not to be confused with the Natraj tandoori a few doors down. Opposite the Shangri-La hotel on Lazimpat.

restaurant.name: Wunjala Moskva
restaurant.text: Tucked away in Naxal district, delicious Newari food in a beautiful setting; performances on the courtyard of the restaurant, and unlimited shots of local booze.

restaurant.name: OR2K
restaurant.text: It is Israeli-run and has a wide variety of good, safe vegetarian food, especially good if you are craving a salad.

restaurant.name: Alchemy
restaurant.text: An Italian restaurant. Somewhat expensive for Thamel. Excellent Italian dishes and nothing else. Pizzas from Rs300 and pastas from Rs280. Cappuccinos. You get wine in 1/4 or 1/2 litre so suitable for dining alone or in two. It's about 100 m before Chetrapati Chowk.

cafe.name: Northfield Cafe
cafe.text: Basic pub grub and Nepali attempt at Mexican, often with live traditional music. Popular with English teachers and expats.

cafe.name: Roadhouse Cafe
cafe.text: Excellent wood fired pizza. Pleasant decor with good coffee & hot chocolate & more cappuccinos. Draught Everest beer, when available. A relaxing, upscale place for when you need to escape from Kathmandu for an evening. Free Wi-Fi.

cafe.name: Irish Pub Lazimpat
cafe.text: Irish dishes, a great variety of beer (also Guinness) and whisky (international and local), Irish Coffee (also Creamy Irish Coffee) cocktails, mocktails, energy cocktails, summer cocktails, shooters (try "Irish Flag"). During the cold season, you can also find "hot winter drinks". Friday nights live music, dart.

cafe.name: Himalayan Cafe
cafe.text: Clean cafe offering traditional Tibetan & Western breakfast, lunch & dinner. Cafe is above Buddhist shop & is on 3, 4 & 5th floors overlooking the stupa. Excellent veggie burger with fried for Rs120. Small pot of milk tea Rs75. Wi-Fi.

cafe.name: Organic Smoothie Bowl and Cafe
cafe.text: Excellent meals prepared with organic ingredients. Sourdough bread. Healthy and tasty smoothies. Polite and quick service. Dull, uninspired interior.

cafe.name: Angan
cafe.text: on the corner behind the King's statue roundabout. A good place to have ice cream (NPR35), Indian traditional sweets or freshly prepared Masala Dhosa which is curry in a crisp savory crêpe, NPR65-75. Sweets in the front, fast food restaurant in the back. The bhel poori is spicy.

cafe.name: Pizza Express
cafe.text: While not quite on par with Roadhouse Cafe or Fire and Ice, Pizza Express makes a tasty product from their locations in Lazimpat (216-1212) and in Basantbur Plaza (423-2777). They are unique in that they are the only mainstream pizza shop with delivery in Kathmandu.

cafe.name: Gupta
cafe.text: A local restaurant that serves South Indian snacks, Indian dishes, and traditional Indian desserts. It is clean, has friendly staff and is very cheap.

cafe.name: Ace Cafe and Bar
cafe.text: Good mix of Indian, Nepali and Western. Costs generally Rs50-120. On the first non-touristy street West of Thamel, across from the People's College.

cafe.name: Cafe Kaldi
cafe.text: has a small menu with drinks, salads & snacks as well as free Wi-Fi for customers (please refrain from downloading anything as the connection is limited.) On Mandala Street, behind OR2K.

cafe.name: Café Mitra
cafe.text: Serves excellent European meals. It is expensive for Kathmandu, but the standard of the food more than makes up for this. 250/13 Thamel Marg.

cafe.name: Just Juice and Shakes
cafe.text: Popular with Israelis and long-timers. Great coffees, fruit juices and shakes. Two eggs on toast: Rs80 in 2012. It can be found 10 m down the alley across the street from the music shop, near Pilgrim's bookshop curve.

photo.name: Garden of Dreams
photo.text: Relax in this beautiful and peaceful walled garden close to Thamel and the former Royal Palace. Beautifully renovated in partnership with the Austrian government. It has two pavilions depicting two of the six annual seasons in the Hindu calendar. There is a mini exhibition showing old photos of this garden.
photo.price: Rs400 for non-Nepalese, Rs150 for Nepalese

photo.name: Shechen Monastery
photo.area: in the alleys near the stupa
photo.text: A very spacious and beautiful temple founded by the late Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. There is a garden restaurant near the monastery guest house.

photo.name: Asa Archives
photo.text: Specialising in medieval history and religious traditions of the Kathmandu Valley. The archives have a collection of some 6,000 loose-leaf handwritten books and 1,000 palm-leaf manuscripts and a manuscript dated to 1464.

Pokhara.name: Pokhara
Pokhara.tagline: Pokhara is the second largest city in Nepal with about 520,000 people in 2021.

info.intro: Pokhara is the second largest city in Nepal with about 520,000 people in 2021. It is the starting point for most of the treks in the Annapurna area. It is a very popular location with most people staying around the beautiful Fewa Lake. Dozens of hotels and restaurants are sprouting like mushrooms everywhere, and today it is much easier to find modern amenities not common to other locations in Nepal, but Pokhara is losing its small town charm and the lakeside now feels more like Khao San Road (with all the usual: yoga, reiki, massages by blind people, overpriced souvenirs and disingenuous locals).
info.get_in: By bus From Kathmandu Tourist buses (Rs700-800, 6-7 hr) and crowded local buses/microbuses (Rs400-600, 6-7 hr) travel the 200-km journey between Kathmandu and Pokhara almost every 15 minutes from 07:30 until late afternoon. Night buses are available, but the ride is painful. Greenline operates a convenient bus every morning between the popular tourist areas of Thamel in Kathmandu and Lakeside in Pokhara (US$20, lunch included). Swift operates comfortable tourist buses for US$15 per ride. The bus runs twice daily, leaving in the morning and in the evening. Swift buses offer comfortable, reclining and extra-wide seats (three per row). The road is winding with many switchbacks but offers wonderful views of hills and rural Nepalese lifestyle.
info.get_around: By foot Pokhara is a mid-sized city and can be traversed on cycle or car or bike. Walking is necessary to get to places where vehicles or bicycles can't reach. By bus Buses and minivans operate on most of the popular routes. These are crowded and uncomfortable but the fare is cheap and student discounts may be offered. Fare is Rs20–40 per way (as of March 2023). By taxi Comfortable taxis are available to be hired. You may also use InDrive app to hail a taxi or motorbike. By bicycle Bicycles can be hired in a lot of shops in Lakeside (Rs300-2,000/day). Make sure the seat is not too hard, and try realigning the seat if it is set uphill way, instead of sloping down. By motorbike or scooter It is also possible to hire a scooter or a motorbike in Lakeside (from Rs550/day). You will have to buy petrol (Rs120/litre).

attraction.name: Devi's Falls (Patale Chhango)
attraction.text: Spectacular, especially after heavy rains. Devi's Falls plunge into a cave and disappear into the earth. The name is from a Swiss couple who were washed away (or fell in) and drowned.

attraction.name: World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa)
attraction.text: Opened in 1999 on top of a hill just south of Phewa Tal, the Stupa offers great views of the Annapurna Mountains, including Fishtail, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Annapurna III. This is a great place to watch the sunrise or sunset over Pokhara.

attraction.name: Mahendra Cave
attraction.text: Bigger than the Bat Cave, however you will need an extra guide to see the hidden parts (will involve some climbing and very narrow passages, only for the adventurous types).
attraction.price: Foreigners Rs150, SAARC citizens Rs80, Nepalis Rs50

attraction.name: Phewa/Fewa Lake (Phewa/Fewa Tal)
attraction.text: One of Nepal's most beautiful spots, Phewa Tal is surrounded by a combination of monkey-filled forests and high white peaks. The reflections in the mirror-like water in the early mornings are impressive.

attraction.name: Begnas Lake (Begnas Tal)
attraction.area: 13.3 km south-east from Pokhara, along the Prithvi Rajmarg road
attraction.text: Out of town and away from the hustle, Begnas Tal is quiet, clean and peaceful. There are a few basic hotels nearby and the odd refreshment shop. A very nice Vipassana Meditation Retreat is also here, one of many around the world.

attraction.name: Rupa Lake (Rupa Tal)
attraction.area: 15 km south-east from Pokhara, along the Prithvi Rajmarg road
attraction.text: One of the more remote lakes in Pokhara with limited accessibility and hence more serene and unspoiled compared to the other lakes. A must visit for any nature lover.

attraction.name: Dipang Lake (Dipang Tal)
attraction.area: 12.7 km south-east from Pokhara, along the Prithvi Rajmarg road
attraction.text: Beautiful lake where you can find wild lotus and wild swan. It is about 25 minutes walk from Sisuwa, the city centre of Lekhnath municipality.

attraction.name: Sarangkot
attraction.text: The perfect pre-trek warm-up. Head up Sarangkot, and be prepared as it's steep and hard work. You can rent a motor bike or use the cable car to go to the top. The road is rough, but traversable.
attraction.price: Cable car: Rs660 single trip, Rs1185 return

attraction.name: Kahun Dharahara
attraction.text: Kahun is the second nearest hill close to the city. At the top of Kahun there's a view tower locally called "Kahun Dharhara". You can get there by bus, motorbike or cycle. Hiking also shouldn't take more than 2 hours to reach there from Ranipauwa.

attraction.name: Dhiki Danda
attraction.text: One of the hills that provides a closer view to the Himalayas. Located on the north of Mahendra Cave, one can reach it by hiking 2-3 hours all the way through Armala. The trail is about 5 km from Mahendra Cave. Beautiful scenery can be observed form the top.

attraction.name: Bat Cave
attraction.area: 10 minutes south from the famous Mahendra cave
attraction.text: This cave is famous for the bats that can be seen hanging from the ceilings.
attraction.price: Foreigners Rs150, SAARC citizens Rs80, Nepalis Rs50

attraction.name: Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave
attraction.area: south of Damside near Devi's Falls
attraction.text: Contains a large stalagmite venerated as a representation of Shiva; two caverns: one the temple and the other leading to a spot near Devi's Falls.

restaurant.name: Asian Teahouse
restaurant.text: Located along the main road through Lakeside on the opposite side from the lake. The only way you'll find this place is to look out for the handwritten sign sitting at the end of the alleyway that the restaurant sits in.

restaurant.name: Sun Welcome
restaurant.text: Small family-run place 5 min north of the main strip, a few spots up from Newari. Cheap and delicious. Open all day, can even BYO.

restaurant.name: Sweet Memories Restaurant
restaurant.text: Nice food with friendly staff.

restaurant.name: Tara's Restaurant (Nepalese Vegetarian)
restaurant.text: A lovely small budget restaurant with a friendly proprietress. A great western-style breakfast with excellent hashbrowns; try the speciality dish, Simi Nariwal.

restaurant.name: El Bocaito Español Spanish Restaurant
restaurant.text: Good and reasonably priced Spanish food. Pleasant atmosphere with Spanish owner.

restaurant.name: Lemon Grass
restaurant.text: Nice restaurant with lake views on the north end of Lakeside.

restaurant.name: Moondance
restaurant.text: A popular place to eat, and although the prices are high so is the quality.

restaurant.name: Natssul Korean Restaurant
restaurant.text: Next to Lakeview Resort towards the tourist bus stand end of town, this is an outdoor garden restaurant run by a Korean couple and serves authentic Korean dishes. Recommended are Vege Bibimbob Hotpot, Beef Bulgogi stew and pork skewers. Free Wi-Fi and the complimentary side dishes are lovely.

restaurant.name: Once upon a time
restaurant.text: Italian and Indian cuisine, very old restaurant in Pokhara. Free Wi-Fi.

restaurant.name: Peace Dragon Lodge and Restaurant
restaurant.text: Serves a good range of Nepali, Indian & Western dishes and light snacks. Prices are moderate, and the views are stunning.

restaurant.name: Pokhara Thakali Kitchen
restaurant.text: Authentic Thakali meals (including Daal Bhat) served on a large platter with several different curries. One of the best places to eat in Pokhara if you're looking for authentic regional dishes.

restaurant.name: Wheat to Sweet
restaurant.text: This place sells tasty buns.

cafe.name: Pokhara Java Coffee House
cafe.text: Nice and cosy coffee place, that serves breakfast, sandwiches and different varieties of coffee. Their set breakfast includes eggs, toast, hash browns and espresso coffee.

cafe.name: Busy Bee Cafe
cafe.text: A beautiful outdoor garden bar, with Pokhara's best rock & roll acts on stage around 20:00.

cafe.name: German Bakery
cafe.text: Another location of this popular bakery chain. This one is especially good if you're walking into town from the airport or on your way to or from the hike to the World Peace Pagoda. Several tables, free Wi-Fi, good breakfasts including honey curd muesli as well as the usual bakery items.

cafe.name: Perky Beans Cafe
cafe.text: Popular place to eat, good breakfast, chapati wraps and renowned 500 ml shakes and smoothies.

cafe.name: Coffee Culture Cafe
cafe.text: Various types of espressos, and other hot and cold drinks. The only completely dedicated organic coffee shop in Pokhara.

cafe.name: Cafe Fusion Restaurant and Bar
cafe.text: Chilled beer, variety of wine, spirits and soft drinks such as smoothies, cocktails and mocktails.

photo.area: off footpath from Lakeside Road in North Lakeside
photo.text: Offers free daily meditation classes, dharma talks and donation-based hatha yoga instruction.

stops.name: Khopoli
stops.text: Khopoli is an industrial town of 109,000 people (2011) in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, at the base of the Sahyadri mountains. Patalganga River flows through Khopoli. The city is called a city of waterfalls due to the number of waterfalls in the rainy season.

stops.name: Matheran
stops.text: Matheran is the closest hill station to Mumbai. It is in the Raigad district of Maharashtra. There are a number of lookout points that provide spectacular views of the surrounding hills and valleys.

stops.name: Mahad
stops.text: Mahad is a town in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, India. So many people have this wrong impression that it is famous for Ganesh Temple which is one of the 8 Ashtavinayak temples, but there are two cities having similar names. The town which comes in Raigad district is not a place among the Ashtavinayak.

stops.name: Dapoli
stops.text: Dapoli is popular beach destination in the South Konkan region of Maharashtra. It is famous for its Agricultural College. Natural beauty of Konkan has lured many people from the literary world. Dapoli served as backdrop of famous Marathi novel Garambicha Bappu by Shri Na. Pendse. Shyamchi aai by Sane Guruji too describes Dapoli.

eat.name: Seafood
eat.text: fish, prawns, oysters, crabs

stops.name: Guhagar
stops.text: Guhagar is a city in the South Konkan region of Maharashtra, India.

stops.name: Marleshwar
stops.text: Marleshwar is a place in Sangameshwar subdivision of Ratnagiri district in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Marleshwar is known for the Cave Shiva Temple.

stops.name: Khadikolvan
stops.text: Khadikolvan is a historic and culturally significant village in the Sangameshwar Taluka of Ratnagiri district, South Konkan, Maharashtra, India. The village is known for its traditional temples, hot springs, and proximity to the famous Marleshwar Temple.

stops.name: Devgad
stops.text: Devgad is a coastal town consisting of 98 villages on the Arabian Sea in Maharashtra, India. It is noted for its harbour, its beach, and a lighthouse built in 1915 at the Devgad fort.

stops.name: Malvan
stops.text: Malvan is a fishing port town of 19,000 people (2011) in the Konkan region of Maharashtra. Malvan has a very nice sea-shore. But it is mainly known for famous Sindhudurg fort. Maratha king Shri Shivaji Maharaj built this fort on island of Kurte.

stops.name: Mandu
stops.text: Mandu or Mandav, literally meaning the "City of Joy", is a small town in the state of Madhya Pradesh in India, now best known for a fort built by Baaz Bahadur in the memory of his queen Rani Roopmati. Between 1401 and 1561 it was the an important citadel of a Muslim rulers of central and north India.

eat.name: Shivani Restaurant
eat.text: While the quality and hit-and-miss, it does serve dishes from the local region including Dal Bafla.

stops.name: Sarangkheda
stops.text: Sarangkheda is a village in North Maharashtra India.

stops.name: Dhule
stops.text: Dhule is a city in North Maharashtra in India.

eat.name: Misal pao
eat.text: It is available in cheap rates and famous for the breakfast of Dhule people.

stops.name: Ahmednagar
stops.text: Ahmednagar, officially Ahilyanagar, has more than 500 years history traced back to 1490, with find traces of Nizamshahi, Shah Jahan and Peshwas until the British took over Ahmednagar.

eat.name: Sweet Home
eat.text: Nice restaurant that serves tasty food.

stops.text: Belgaum or Belgaon, officially Belagavi, is a city in Northwestern Karnataka, neighbouring to the state of Goa and Maharashtra, deeply embroiled in claims over this district. eat.name: Venketeshwara Cafe

stops.name: Davanagere
stops.text: Davanagere is a city in Central Karnataka. Davanagere is known for its business. Crop business is a most common source of income here.

stops.name: Dharwad
stops.text: Dharwad or Dharwar is in the northern part of Karnataka state, in South India. It's known for its numerous world class universities and colleges.

stops.name: Dandeli
stops.text: Dandeli is a small town in the western ghats of North-West Karnataka, India. Dandeli is known as a wildlife sanctuary and is proud of being one of the tiger projects. People have also moved from across India to work in the industries in Dandeli. Dandeli is also known for its adventure activities on the River Kali.

stops.text: Palghar and Kelve are two towns on the North Konkan coast of Maharashtra. There are several forts in and around the two towns.

stops.name: Valsad
stops.text: Valsad is a city of 170,000 people (2011) in the Indian state Gujarat. It used to be called Bulsar and be the administrative capital of Valsad district. It's famous for its mango orchards and an increasingly popular destination with a nice beach and several temples.

eat.name: Raja Rani Wada Pav
eat.text: Very famous for the Wada Pav.

stops.name: Surat
stops.text: Surat, a bustling commercial city in South Gujarat, is a major gemstone centre with over 92% of the world's diamonds being cut here. On the banks of the Tapi River, Surat was a major port in medieval India as well as the early British colonial times till the formation of the city of Bombay (present-day Mumbai).

eat.name: Saurashtra Bakery

stops.name: Bannerghatta National Park
stops.text: Bannerghatta National Park is a national park south of Bengaluru, in Southeastern Karnataka. It is a popular tourist destination with a zoo, a pet corner, an animal rescue centre, a butterfly enclosure, an aquarium, a snake house and a safari park. You can find everything from avifauna to panthers (tigers, lions, leopards) in the national park.

Another important trade activity is tobacco growing and tobacco auctions. There is a tobacco board in Kattemalalavadi which is 5 km from the city. Consolidated Coffee Curing Works employs many people in coffee bean processing.
